page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 20 physical cores and 20 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, running under a KVM hypervisor. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 12.8 GB of RAM per core. Graphics and parallel computing acceleration are delivered by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU from the Ada Lovelace architecture, which includes 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly robust, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 3960.24 GB/sec and uncached large block reads at 309.72 GB/sec. The instance excels in specialized tasks, achieving top-tier results in image processing, text processing, and single-threaded compression. LLM inference benchmarks show top-tier performance for small 135M models, while medium 7B and large 70B models deliver strong to average processing speeds.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers high resource density by pairing a top-tier AMD EPYC processor with a high-VRAM NVIDIA L40S GPU, making it a viable option for compute-heavy and memory-intensive tasks without requiring multi-GPU deployments. However, the lack of local storage requires external storage solutions, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This server is highly suited for GPU-accelerated workloads, machine learning and LLM inference, image processing, and high-performance computing tasks.
description: The UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-1xL40S is a high-performance, GPU-accelerated server designed for demanding computational workloads. It features 20 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor, 256.0 GB of RAM, and a single NVIDIA L40S GPU with 48 GB of VRAM. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under a KVM hypervisor, the instance delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong multi-core capabilities. While it lacks local storage, its memory bandwidth and processing speeds are highly competitive, particularly for image processing, text processing, and small-to-medium LLM inference. This hardware profile makes the server well-suited for machine learning, data science, and compute-heavy parallel processing tasks.
